open_points.subject: AdmissionVerdict identity and repeated admission
open_points.text: “trial_executions: the TrialExecutions (M07) this admission ran” and “every active case of the corpus is run again for the implementation at admission time” conflict with “a verdict for the same implementation and corpus is the same verdict”; each rerun mints different TrialExecution entities.
open_points.question: When the same implementation is admitted again over the unchanged corpus, is the existing AdmissionVerdict reused, or is a new verdict created with newly minted trial executions?
options: Reuse the existing verdict and its executions
Run new executions and create a distinct verdict
Run new executions but replace or merge evidence into the same verdict
open_points.default_guess: Reuse the existing verdict while the implementation and corpus digest are unchanged.

open_points.subject: ProofResult identity under changing binding status
open_points.text: “Substitution: proving the same version gives the same result” conflicts with the carried rule that “a flow version whose proof failed because a binding was not yet accepted can be proven again later — closed by A05 (yes).”
open_points.question: What distinguishes two ProofResults for the same immutable flow version when acceptance of a referenced binding changes the result?
options: ProofResult identity includes the relevant binding-state snapshot
Each computation is a separate result entity
ProofResult is only the current replaceable result for a flow version
open_points.default_guess: Treat each computed result as a value of all its result facts plus the dependency state against which proof was performed.

open_points.subject: Agent Actor identity after token removal
open_points.text: “agent_name” is the only agent identity fact, while “revoking an agent is removing its token”; the text does not say whether a removed agent name may later be assigned to another token or principal.
open_points.question: If an agent token is removed and a token with the same agent name is later configured, do historical and new records identify the same Actor?
options: The name is permanently bound to one actor and may only be reused for that actor
Reusing the name always denotes the same actor regardless of token
A new token or configuration generation creates a new actor identity
open_points.default_guess: Treat the agent name as the stable actor identity, so reuse denotes the same actor.

open_points.subject: EffectAttempt unknown-resolution timestamps
open_points.text: EffectAttempt carries only “recorded_at, concluded_at” and “resolved_by”, although its lifecycle has both “in_flight → unknown” and the later transition “unknown → applied | not_applied by the owner.”
open_points.question: For an attempt first recorded as unknown and later resolved, what event does concluded_at record, and is the time of the owner's resolution itself retained?
options: concluded_at records entry into unknown and a separate resolved_at records resolution
concluded_at is absent while unknown and records the later owner resolution
concluded_at is overwritten when the owner resolves the attempt
The resolution time is not retained
open_points.default_guess: Keep concluded_at as the time the send became unknown and retain a separate resolved_at for the owner's resolution.
